About INCB161734

INCB161734 is an investigational, novel, selective and orally bioavailable small molecule ON/OFF KRAS G12D inhibitor. KRAS is one of the most frequently altered oncogenic drivers across solid tumors, and the KRAS G12D mutation is among the most common KRAS alterations, occurring in approximately 40% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cases and approximately 15% of colorectal cancer (CRC) cases.

It is currently being investigated in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and other solid tumors, including colorectal cancer (CRC). Key Terms

kras g12d inhibitormedical
A KRAS G12D inhibitor is a targeted anti-cancer drug that selectively binds to and blocks the abnormal KRAS protein carrying the G12D mutation (an aspartic acid substituting glycine at amino-acid position 12). By preventing the mutant KRAS protein from activating downstream growth-signaling pathways, these inhibitors aim to stop or slow tumor cell proliferation driven specifically by the G12D variant. They are mutation-specific therapies and generally do not inhibit wild-type KRAS or other KRAS mutations, and their effectiveness depends on the tumor actually being driven by the KRAS G12D alteration and on the drug’s ability to reach and engage the mutant protein in cancer cells.
igg1-bispecific antibodymedical
A IgG1-bispecific antibody is a single engineered antibody molecule built on the human IgG1 scaffold that can bind two different antigens or two different sites on the same antigen at once. Because it uses the IgG1 backbone, it typically includes the Fc region that can be left intact or modified to tune properties like serum half-life and immune effector functions; functionally, bispecifics can simultaneously block two biological targets or physically bring two cell types together (for example, a cancer cell and a T cell). As a class they are distinct from ordinary monoclonal antibodies in that one molecule has dual specificity, and they often require specialized manufacturing and regulatory considerations due to their complexity and engineered features.
lgr5medical
LGR5 is a gene that encodes a cell-surface receptor protein (Leucine-rich repeat–containing G protein–coupled receptor 5) commonly used as a marker of adult stem cells in several tissues, especially the intestine and hair follicles. The protein sits on the cell membrane and helps cells respond to signaling molecules that regulate regeneration and self-renewal; researchers use its presence to identify, isolate, or target stem-like cells in both normal tissue and certain tumors. Its role can vary by tissue and context, so detecting LGR5 indicates a stem-like or progenitor cell state but does not uniquely define cell function or clinical behavior.

  • IMA402 PRAME bispecific continues to demonstrate encouraging anti-tumor activity in multiple indications, alongside a favorable safety profile

  • IMA402 achieved a cORR of 32%, 12.5 months median DOR and a 1-year OS rate of 91% in advanced melanoma patients with high PRAME expression

  • Clinical profile of IMA402 reinforces development path across multiple solid tumor indications, including melanoma, gynecologic cancers and lung cancer, in earlier and later treatment lines, supported by Immatics’ innovative, rapid liquid biopsy-based PRAME testing

  • IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy demonstrated deep and durable anti-tumor activity across multiple tumor types with a manageable safety profile, supporting its tumor-agnostic potential. At clinically relevant dose levels in patients with advanced, heavily pretreated gynecologic cancers, cORR was 55% with a median DOR of 8.4 months

Houston, Texas and Tuebingen, Germany, October 24, 2026 – Immatics N.V. (NASDAQ: IMTX, “Immatics” or the “Company”), the global leader in precision targeting of PRAME with multiple clinical-stage programs spanning cell therapies and bispecifics, today announced updated clinical trial data from its ongoing Phase 1b study with IMA402 PRAME bispecific and its Phase 1 study with IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy.

The IMA402 data will be presented in a rapid oral presentation (1955RO) by Dirk Schadendorf, M.D., and the IMA203CD8 data were presented in an oral presentation (1946O) by Antonia Busse, M.D., at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) in Madrid, Spain. In addition, exploratory analyses of the anzu-cel Phase 1b melanoma cohort will be presented in a poster (2128P) by Sapna Patel, M.D. The slides are available in the ‘Events & Presentations’ section of the Investor & Media page on the Company’s website.

“The data presented at ESMO further underscore the potential of IMA402 as an off-the-shelf treatment option for patients with solid cancers. This promising clinical profile reinforces our strategy as we continue to advance IMA402 across multiple cancer types and treatment lines, with combination approaches further expanding its reach,” said Cedrik Britten, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Medical Officer at Immatics. “In addition, as the IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy data continue to mature, we are increasingly encouraged by its broad potential for patients with advanced PRAME-positive cancers. Together with anzu-cel, IMA402 and IMA203CD8 give us three distinct and complementary approaches to target PRAME, with the potential to reach more patients across a broad range of cancers.”

Rapid Oral Presentation Summary - IMA402 PRAME TCR Bispecific Phase 1b Trial

Patient Population: Heavily pretreated patient population with a median of 3 prior lines of therapy
As of the data cutoff on June 1, 2026, 126 heavily pretreated patients across multiple tumor types, primarily melanoma and ovarian cancer, received at least one infusion of IMA402 during the dose escalation or dose expansion part of the ongoing trial (NCT05958121). Patients had received a median of 3 prior lines of systemic treatment, had a median target lesion sum of diameter of 7.4 cm and had a median of 4 tumor lesions. The efficacy population included 40 patients treated within the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) range of 10 to 45 mg across varying levels of PRAME expression. Within this population, 31 patients exhibited high PRAME expression levels (PRAME-high)1 in their tumors. Of these, all patients with PRAME-high melanoma had received prior systemic treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI), with a median of 2 prior ICI regimens and all patients with PRAME-high ovarian cancer were previously treated with platinum-based chemotherapy.

Safety: Favorable tolerability profile as monotherapy and as combination therapy
IMA402 showed favorable tolerability across all doses. The most frequent treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were expected, transient lymphopenia and low-grade cytokine release syndrome (CRS), consistent with the mechanism of action. No cases of ICANS were reported. No IMA402-related Grade 5 events were reported. Tolerability was consistent across all evaluated doses, including the RP2D range, with no additive toxicity observed when combined with an ICI.

Anti-tumor Activity and Durability: 32% cORR in PRAME-high melanoma with promising durability and survival
IMA402 showed promising anti-tumor activity as monotherapy (n=36) or in combination with an immune checkpoint inhibitor (n=4) in the efficacy population at RP2D range. Treatment with IMA402 demonstrated 10 confirmed responses resulting in an overall confirmed objective response rate (cORR) of 25% (10/40) and a disease control rate (DCR) of 63% (25/40). This includes one confirmed complete response in melanoma. The longest ongoing response exceeded 2 years. In the PRAME-high population, cORR was 32% (10/31) across all indications and 32% (7/22) in patients with melanoma. The PRAME-high melanoma population further showed a median duration of response (mDOR) of 12.5 months (median follow-up, mFU, 16.8 months). Median overall survival (mOS) was not reached (mFU 8.8 months), with 91% of patients alive at 1 year (versus 60% of patients treated below RP2D range), indicating promising overall survival data irrespective of best response. Among 6 patients with PRAME-high ovarian cancer, 3 confirmed responses were reported.

Next Development Steps for IMA402:
The promising clinical profile of IMA402 supports a development path across various solid tumors in earlier and later treatment lines. These include combination approaches with ICIs in melanoma and in gynecologic cancers as well as IMA402 in combination with the Company’s MAGEA4/8-directed bispecific, IMA401, in lung cancer with first data expected in 2027. Furthermore, the use of Immatics’ proprietary rapid, sensitive and reliable liquid biopsy-based PRAME testing enables precise patient selection and could support potential fast-to-market strategies, subject to regulatory approval, in PRAME-high melanoma and beyond.

Oral Presentation Summary - IMA203CD8 PRAME Cell Therapy Phase 1 Trial

Patient population: Heavily pretreated patient population with limited treatment options
As of the data cutoff on August 7, 2026, 98 heavily pretreated patients across multiple advanced solid tumor types expressing PRAME that had undergone a median of 3 prior systemic treatments were enrolled in the ongoing Phase 1 dose escalation/dose expansion trial (NCT03686124). Of these, 90 patients were evaluable for efficacy, including 27 with gynecologic cancers (ovarian and uterine cancer), 44 with melanoma, 12 with synovial sarcoma and 7 with other solid tumor types. All patients with ovarian cancer had received prior platinum-based therapy.

Safety: Treatment with IMA203CD8 was manageable
IMA203CD8 demonstrated a consistent and manageable safety profile across different solid tumor types and a wide dose range (median dose 1.81x109 TCR T cells, range 0.44-12.50x109). The most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were expected and included transient cytopenias associated with the lymphodepletion regimen and low-grade cytokine release syndrome (CRS), consistent with the mechanism of action. ICANS was infrequently observed, and no IMA203CD8-related Grade 5 events occurred. Maximum tolerated dose (MTD) was not reached with doses up to 12.5 billion IMA203CD8 cells.

Anti-tumor Activity and Durability: One-time infusion of IMA203CD8 PRAME cell therapy showed anti-tumor activity across multiple tumor types
Across all evaluated dose levels and tumor types, including lower dose levels not selected for further clinical development, a one-time infusion of IMA203CD8 demonstrated an ORR of 51% (46/90) and a cORR of 41% (36/87). The DCR was 82% (74/90) and 83% (71/86) of patients with evaluable target lesions experienced tumor reduction. Responses were observed across multiple solid tumors expressing PRAME, including ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, melanoma, synovial sarcoma, and others. Durable long-term responses were observed with ongoing responses for more than 2.5 years.

In 20 patients with gynecologic cancers (ovarian and uterine cancer) treated at clinically relevant dose levels (≥DL4c), IMA203CD8 demonstrated consistent anti-tumor activity with an ORR of 60% (12/20) and a cORR of 55% (11/20), a DCR of 70% (14/20) and tumor reduction in 68% (13/19) of patients. Early durability data showed a mDOR of 8.4 months (mFU 6.0 months), a mPFS of 5.8 months (mFU 8.1 months) and mOS not reached at 7.8 months mFU.

Next Development Steps for IMA203CD8:
Phase 1a dose escalation is complete. Immatics is currently enrolling patients with uterine cancer at clinically relevant doses to further expand the clinical dataset in this indication. In addition, a Phase 1/2 investigator-initiated trial (IIT) in patients with PRAME-positive pediatric cancers is planned to start in 1H 2027. The clinical activity of IMA203CD8 observed across tumor types with distinct biology and differing levels of PRAME expression, including ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, melanoma and synovial sarcoma, supports the broad applicability of IMA203CD8 across PRAME-positive cancers. The development approach for IMA203CD8 will leverage targeted cohorts of selected tumor types, such as ovarian cancer, uterine cancer, rare cancers and pediatric cancers to build the clinical evidence base for broader, tumor-agnostic application.

Poster Presentation Summary – Anzu-cel Phase 1b Melanoma Cohort
Additional exploratory analyses (data cutoff Sept 24, 2025) of anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel, IMA203), presented in a poster (2128P) by Sapna Patel, M.D., demonstrated durable clinical benefit following a one-time treatment in a heavily pretreated population of patients with advanced melanoma. Durable clinical benefit was observed across patients with varied baseline clinical and treatment characteristics, with no single characteristic identified as a predictor of prolonged PFS. Exploratory analyses suggested that lower tumor burden, lower LDH, and a higher effector-to-target ratio may be associated with longer PFS. These findings further strengthen the clinical profile of anzu-cel, which is currently being evaluated in the Phase 3 SUPRAME trial in advanced melanoma.

About IMA402 PRAME Bispecific
IMA402 is a molecule from Immatics’ TCR bispecifics (TCER®) pipeline directed against an HLA-A*02:01-presented peptide derived from PRAME. IMA402 is currently being evaluated in a Phase 1b clinical trial in patients with solid tumors expressing PRAME. IMA402 is part of Immatics’ strategy to leverage the full clinical potential of targeting PRAME, one of the most promising targets for TCR-based therapies.

About IMA203CD8 PRAME Cell Therapy
IMA203CD8 is Immatics’ PRAME-directed TCR T-cell therapy engineered to recognize an intracellular PRAME-derived peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 on the cell surface and initiate a potent and specific anti-tumor response. Co-transduction of CD8αβ with the PRAME TCR adds functional CD4+ T cells designed to boost anti-tumor activity. IMA203CD8 is currently being evaluated in a Phase 1b clinical trial in solid tumors expressing PRAME.

About Anzu-cel PRAME Cell Therapy
Anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel; IMA203) is a PRAME-directed TCR T-cell therapy engineered to recognize an intracellular PRAME-derived peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 on the cell surface and initiate a potent and specific anti-tumor response. Anzu-cel PRAME cell therapy is currently being evaluated in a registration-enabling randomized controlled Phase 3 trial, “SUPRAME,” in patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma who have disease progression on or after treatment with at least one checkpoint inhibitor. In parallel, the Phase 1/2 clinical trial is ongoing with a focus on uveal melanoma.

About PRAME
PRAME is a tumor-associated target expressed in more than 50 cancers. Immatics’ PRAME franchise includes multiple product candidates, therapeutic modalities, indications and combination approaches: anzu-cel (anzutresgene autoleucel; IMA203) and IMA203CD8, both PRAME-directed cell therapies, and IMA402, a PRAME-directed bispecific. Combination approaches include IMA402 with immune checkpoint inhibitors, IMA402 with the MAGEA4/8-directed bispecific IMA401, and anzu-cel in combination with Moderna’s PRAME mRNA therapy designed to enhance the cell therapy response.

Immatics is committed to making a meaningful impact on the lives of patients with cancer. We are the global leader in precision targeting of PRAME, a target expressed in more than 50 cancers. Our cutting-edge science and robust clinical pipeline form the broadest PRAME franchise with the most PRAME indications and modalities, spanning TCR T-cell therapies and TCR bispecifics.

AirLink 5G Solutions Keep First Responders Connected During Peak Network Demand

CAMARILLO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Semtech Corporation (Nasdaq: SMTC), a leading provider of high-performance semiconductors powering AI data center networking and intelligent, connected Internet of Things (“IoT”) devices worldwide, is adding new resilient communications building blocks to its AirLink® 5G Networking Solutions. Semtech will demonstrate the new capabilities in booth #2964 at the International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP) conference in Orlando, Fla.

Semtech’s AirLink XR60, XR80 and XR90 in-vehicle 5G routers support network slicing, FIPS 140-3 and fleet management for public safety agencies.

First responders rely on in-vehicle connectivity for computer-aided dispatch, live video and mobile data. When a mass-casualty incident, large-scale event or natural disaster pushes commercial networks to capacity, public safety traffic can get caught in the same congestion. In a recent survey, 64% of first responders named unreliable network connectivity as their single biggest concern (Source: T-Mobile, “5G and Public Safety: Transforming Emergency Response with T-Priority,” T-Mobile Newsroom, 2025).

“Resilient communication is not a capacity problem; it’s a priority and a data security problem,” said Kinana Hussein, vice president of networking solutions at Semtech. “AirLink networking solutions help address both. Network slicing support gives public safety dedicated, prioritized access to network resources, and AirLink OS 6.1 helps agencies meet FIPS 140-3 through a software update, with no hardware replacement.”

AirLink XR90, XR80 and XR60 Routers

The AirLink XR90, XR80 and XR60 in-vehicle 5G routers are built for public safety fleets. All three are FirstNet Trusted™ for use on FirstNet, built with AT&T, and certified for both T-Mobile’s T-Priority and Verizon’s Frontline network slices, giving agencies dedicated, prioritized access to emergency network resources on either carrier.

FIPS 140-3 and Zero Trust

With the new AirLink OS 6.1 operating system release, compatible AirLink routers can meet the new Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) 140-3 through a software update, with no hardware replacement required. FIPS 140-3 replaces FIPS 140-2, whose certificates the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s Cryptographic Module Validation Program (CMVP) moved to its Historical List on Sept. 21, 2026. Semtech’s Zero Trust architecture builds on its recently announced integration with Palo Alto Networks Next-Generation Firewalls.

Fleet Management Built to Scale

New fleet management groups in Semtech’s AirLink Management Service platform let administrators set the software and configuration standard for each device model, check compliance across the fleet immediately and correct devices that are not configured to the standard. AirLink Manager / AirLink Mobility Manager 2.18.1 extends that flexibility further, adding on-premises management options across the full AirLink OS portfolio, so agencies can manage fleets in the cloud or air-gapped.

Greg Hill, Semtech director of product management, AirLink Networking Solutions, and Dan Robinson, Semtech director of AirLink government sales and a former police chief, will present “5G Network Slicing, Satellite, Zero Trust: The New Building Blocks of Resilient Communications” on Monday, Oct. 26 from 3:15–3:45 PM EDT. Key Terms

network slicingtechnical
Network slicing is a way telecom operators create multiple virtual networks on the same physical infrastructure, each tuned for a specific purpose — like carving a cake into pieces for different tastes: one slice optimized for very fast mobile video, another for highly reliable industrial sensors. It matters to investors because slices let carriers sell tailored, higher-margin services, improve network efficiency and support new business models (enterprise contracts, IoT, critical communications), which can boost recurring revenue and change capital and partnership strategies.
fips 140-3regulatory
A U.S. government standard that sets detailed security requirements for cryptographic modules—software or hardware components that encrypt data and manage keys. Think of it as a rigorous safety inspection for digital locks: passing the test signals that a product meets recognized security practices, which matters to investors because certification can affect a company’s ability to sell to governments and regulated industries, reduce legal and operational risk, and support customer trust.
zero trusttechnical
Zero trust is a security approach that assumes no one, whether inside or outside an organization, should be automatically trusted. Instead, every access request is carefully verified before being granted, much like checking ID at every door rather than trusting someone just because they are known. For investors, it emphasizes the importance of protecting digital assets and data from potential breaches, reducing overall risk.
air-gappedtechnical
A system described as air-gapped is physically isolated from public and private networks so it cannot be reached over the internet or company LAN, like a safe kept in a room with no phone line. For investors this matters because air-gapping reduces the risk that critical data, trading algorithms, backups or industrial controls will be accessed or tampered with by hackers, but it can also increase costs and slow information flow compared with connected systems.

Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) in combination with bevacizumab demonstrated a 79% confirmed objective response rate and 100% disease control rate, with similar activity observed across FRα expression levels

Clinical activity with Sofe-M was maintained even in patients with prior PARP inhibitor exposure, patients who typically experience poor outcomes with platinum-based chemotherapy

Sofe-M is currently being studied in both platinum-sensitive and platinum-resistant ovarian cancer in multiple Phase 3 studies as part of the FRAmework-01 master protocol

INDIANAPOLIS, Oct. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eli Lilly and Company (NYSE: LLY) today announced new Phase 1 data showing that its investigational folate receptor alpha (FRα) antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) plus bevacizumab achieved a confirmed objective response rate (cORR) of 79% and a disease control rate (DCR) of 100% in patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC). A cORR of 79% or higher was seen in both poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi)-treated and PARPi-naïve patients. These data will be shared in an oral presentation at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Annual Congress in Madrid, Spain.

FRα is expressed in almost all ovarian cancers, at much higher levels than in healthy tissue, making it a target that can help direct treatment to tumor cells. Sofe-M is an FRα-targeting ADC composed of an Fc-silent, FRα-specific humanized monoclonal antibody linked to exatecan, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, via a proprietary cleavable polysarcosine linker. The antibody is designed to bind FRα on the surface of tumor cells, delivering exatecan directly into the tumor cell to disrupt DNA replication.

Jacob Van Naarden, Executive Vice President and President of Lilly Oncology: "The standard of care for platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer has remained unchanged for a decade and demands new treatment options. Results for Sofe-M show a promising efficacy and tolerability profile across both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer, regardless of FRα expression levels or prior treatment. These data give us confidence as we continue to study Sofe-M in our Phase 3 FRAmework-01 program to bring this potential new medicine to the women who need it."

The Phase 1 study is evaluating Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in patients with advanced solid tumors, including a cohort of 33 women with PSOC who received Sofe-M (4 mg/kg) plus bevacizumab (15 mg/kg). Patients received a median of three prior systemic regimens (range 1–6), including prior PARPi (67%) and prior bevacizumab (70%). As of the July 6, 2026, data cutoff, the cORR among the 29 patients with measurable disease was 79.3% (23/29; 6 complete responses [CR, 20.7%] and 17 partial responses [PR, 58.6%]), and DCR was 100%. Responses were consistent across FRα expression levels and prior PARPi exposure. Median duration of response (DOR) and median progression-free survival (PFS) were not reached at median follow-ups of 6.2 and 10.2 months, respectively.

Chrisann Kyi, MD, Gynecologic Medical Oncologist & Early Drug Development Specialist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center: "The durable and robust responses we've seen in patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer are important, particularly in a PARPi pretreated population, where the response rate seen with Sofe-M exceeds what has been reported in published platinum re-challenge studies. The observed safety profile and low discontinuation rates, combined with early efficacy results, support the continued investigation of Sofe-M as a potentially meaningful new option for patients."

Sofe-M plus bevacizumab demonstrated a safety profile consistent with the known profiles of each medicine. No new safety signals were observed. The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) across all patients included epistaxis (73%), nausea (73%), anemia (58%), neutropenia (55%), and fatigue (52%). The most common Grade ≥3 TEAEs were neutropenia (42%) and anemia (24%); febrile neutropenia occurred in 3% of patients, and G-CSF prophylaxis was not mandated. Any-grade neuropathy occurred in 9% of patients, with no Grade ≥3 events. Dose reductions occurred in 42% of patients, and 6% discontinued treatment due to an adverse event.

The FRAmework-01 program is evaluating Sofe-M in three global Phase 3 trials across both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer: Part A tests Sofe-M as monotherapy in platinum-resistant disease; Part B tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in platinum-sensitive disease that progressed on or within six months of completing a PARPi; and Part C tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in PARPi-naïve platinum-sensitive disease. The study is being conducted in partnership with the European Network for Gynaecological Oncological Trial groups (ENGOT - lead groups GINECO/NOGGO e.V.), the GOG Foundation (GOG), and the Asia-Pacific Gynecologic Oncology Trials Group (APGOT).

For more information on Lilly's oncology pipeline, click here.

Frequently Asked Questions

  1. What is sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M)?

    Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) is an investigational folate receptor alpha (FRα)-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) being studied for the treatment of ovarian cancer and other solid tumors. It is designed to selectively bind to cancer cells expressing FRα and deliver a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload directly to those cells.

  2. What is an antibody-drug conjugate? 

    An antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) is a type of medicine that pairs an antibody with a cell-killing payload. The antibody is designed to recognize and bind to a specific protein found on the surface of cancer cells, and the payload is released once the ADC reaches its target, allowing the medicine to attack cancer cells while limiting exposure to healthy tissue.1

  3. How is Sofe-M different from other FRα-targeted ADCs? 

    Sofe-M is designed to target FRα across a broad range of expression levels, including in tumors with lower FRα expression. In this Phase 1 study, Sofe-M plus bevacizumab showed a confirmed objective response rate of 79.3% in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC), with consistent activity across FRα expression levels and regardless of prior PARP inhibitor exposure. Earlier studies in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) also demonstrated responses observed across all FRα expression levels and in patients previously treated with mirvetuximab soravtansine (MIRV).2 These results are being further evaluated in Lilly's ongoing Phase 3 FRAmework-01 program, which is studying Sofe-M across both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer.

  4. What are the results with sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) in the treatment of platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)?

    The Phase 1 study demonstrated encouraging clinical activity, including a confirmed objective response rate (cORR) of 79.3% and a disease control rate (DCR) of 100%, in heavily pretreated patients with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer. Activity was observed across FRα expression levels and regardless of prior PARP inhibitor exposure. Median duration of response (DOR) and median progression-free survival (PFS) were not reached at median follow-ups of 6.2 and 10.2 months, respectively. Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) plus bevacizumab demonstrated a safety profile consistent with the known profiles of each medicine, with no new safety signals observed and a low rate of discontinuation due to adverse events (6%). These findings support continued investigation of Sofe-M in the ongoing Phase 3 FRAmework-01 trial.

  5. In this study Sofe-M was dosed at 4 mg/kg. Why is it dosed at 3mg/kg in the Phase 3 FRAmework-01 trial? 

    The 3 mg/kg dose of Sofe-M was selected as the recommended phase 3 dose (RP3D), based on analysis of the safety, efficacy and PK data as monotherapy. The ORR was comparable between the two doses, with ORRs of 59.0% (95% CI 42.1, 74.4) and 58.8% (95% CI 32.9, 81.6), at 4 mg/kg and 3mg/kg doses, respectively. Safety signals were higher at 4 mg/kg versus 3 mg/kg, with Grade ≥3 TRAEs at 56.4% vs 35.3% and dose reductions of 41.0% vs 23.5%.

  6. What are historical clinical trial results for standard of care in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)?

    For patients who recur after platinum-based chemotherapy and PARP inhibitor (PARPi) maintenance, published real world data on subsequent platinum re-challenge have shown modest response rates, with an objective response rate (ORR) of 41.9%.3 Other studies of platinum-based regimens, such as OCEANS, were conducted prior to the routine use of PARPi maintenance and did not include patients previously treated with a PARPi,4 a population that now represents a majority of patients with recurrent PSOC, including those enrolled in Sofe-M's Phase 1 study.

  7. What is platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)? 

    Platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC) is characterized as ovarian cancer that comes back more than six months after platinum-based chemotherapy. While people with PSOC can often be treated with platinum again, the disease tends to return, and each recurrence can leave fewer treatment options and shorter remissions.5

  8. What is the current unmet need in platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)?

    The standard of care for PSOC has remained largely unchanged for more than a decade, even as understanding of which patients benefit from it has evolved. Approximately 50% of PSOC patients have HRD-positive tumors, meaning their tumors carry a specific DNA-repair deficiency.6 These patients tend to have longer progression-free survival with upfront platinum-based chemotherapy plus a PARP inhibitor (PARPi).6 However, when these patients do recur after PARPi maintenance, response rates to subsequent platinum-based treatment are modest.6 Patients with non-HRD-positive tumors see minimal benefit from PARPi to begin with and generally have a poorer prognosis overall.6 Despite these different outcomes between HRD-positive and HRD-negative patients, treatment approaches for PSOC have not meaningfully changed to reflect that distinction.

  9. What is the difference between platinum-resistant (PROC) and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer (PSOC)?

    The difference comes down to timing. If ovarian cancer returns more than six months after platinum-based chemotherapy, it's considered platinum-sensitive, and patients often respond well to platinum treatment again. If the cancer returns within six months, or continues growing during treatment, it's considered platinum-resistant, and platinum-based chemotherapy is generally no longer effective. Because platinum resistance tends to develop gradually, each recurrence can bring a shorter remission, even while a patient's disease is still classified as platinum-sensitive.6

  10. What is folate receptor alpha (FRα), and why is FRα expression level important in treating ovarian cancer?

    FRα is expressed in almost all ovarian cancers, at much higher levels than in healthy tissue, making it a target that can help direct treatment to tumor cells.7 FRα expression level refers to the amount of the protein present on a tumor and may influence eligibility for or response to certain FRα-targeted therapies.7

  11. How is the FRAmework-01 clinical trial designed? 

    FRAmework-01 is a global, three-part Phase 3 trial studying sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) across both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer in a single program: Part A tests Sofe-M as monotherapy in platinum-resistant disease; Part B tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in platinum-sensitive disease that progressed on or within six months of completing a PARPi; and Part C tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in PARPi-naïve platinum-sensitive disease.

    The trial's main measure of success across all three parts is how long patients go without their cancer progressing. The study is being conducted in partnership with the European Network for Gynaecological Oncological Trial groups (ENGOT - lead groups GINECO/NOGGO e.V.), the GOG Foundation (GOG), and the Asia-Pacific Gynecologic Oncology Trials Group (APGOT). Enrollment is ongoing globally with first registrational dose in Q4 2025 for PROC and in Q1 2026 for PSOC.

About Ovarian Cancer

Ovarian cancer is the sixth leading cause of cancer death among women in the United States.8 While most patients initially respond to platinum-based chemotherapy, approximately 70% will experience recurrence, leading to progressively shorter remission periods with each subsequent treatment.6 When cancer recurs during or within six months of platinum therapy, known as platinum-resistant disease, patients face limited treatment options.6,9

About Sofetabart Mipitecan

Sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M; LY4170156) is composed of an Fc-silent, folate receptor alpha (FRα) specific humanized monoclonal antibody linked to exatecan, a topoisomerase I inhibitor, via a proprietary cleavable polysarcosine linker (PSARlink). Sofe-M was designed to target FRα across all expression levels with improved therapeutic index. FRα is a cell-surface glycoprotein encoded by the gene FOLR1 that binds to the essential nutrients folic acid and reduced folates, bringing them into cells to facilitate cell division and growth. FRα is overexpressed in many solid tumors such as ovarian and endometrial cancers. Sofe-M has received Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (PROC) and is currently being evaluated in the Phase 3 FRAmework-01 program. The study is being conducted in partnership with the European Network for Gynaecological Oncological Trial groups (ENGOT - lead groups GINECO/NOGGO e.V.), the GOG Foundation (GOG), and the Asia-Pacific Gynecologic Oncology Trials Group (APGOT).  

About FRAmework-01

FRAmework-01 (NCT07213804) is a Phase 3, randomized, open-label, three-part study evaluating sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M; LY4170156) in patients with recurrent epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer. Part A tests Sofe-M as monotherapy in platinum-resistant disease; Part B tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in platinum-sensitive disease that progressed on or within six months of completing a PARPi; and Part C tests Sofe-M plus bevacizumab in PARPi-naïve platinum-sensitive disease. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival (PFS), assessed by the investigator in Part A and by blinded independent central review (BICR) in Parts B and C. Key secondary endpoints are overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, and safety.  The FRAmework-01 study is in partnership with the European Network for Gynecological Oncological Trial groups (ENGOT - lead groups GINECO/NOGGO e.V.), the GOG Foundation (GOG), and the Asia-Pacific Gynecologic Oncology Trials Group (APGOT).

More information on FRAmework-01 can be found on clinicaltrials.gov.

data.title: ESMO 2026: NUBEQA® (darolutamide) Plus ADT and Radiation Therapy Reduces Risk of Metastasis or Death by 58% in Prostate Cancer Patients at High Risk of Recurrence | BAYRY Stock News
data.description:
Four-year metastasis-free survival reached 95% versus 88% with placebo, while Grade ≥3 adverse events were more frequent.

See more from StockTitan in Google Search and AI answers.Adds StockTitan as a preferred source · opens Google
Add on Google
  • Interim analysis results from the Phase III DASL-HiCaP trial show a statistically significant 58% reduction in the risk of metastasis or death with NUBEQA® (darolutamide) versus placebo in addition to androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and radiation therapy (hazard ratio [HR] 0.42; 95% CI: 0.27–0.66; p=0.0001)
  • Four-year metastasis-free survival rate in trial reached 95% with NUBEQA compared to 88% with placebo, alongside secondary endpoint improvements and a safety profile consistent with previous studies
  • Results will be presented as a late-breaking abstract in a Presidential Symposium at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026

WHIPPANY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--New late-breaking data to be presented today by the Australian and New Zealand Urogenital and Prostate (ANZUP) Clinical Trials Group at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 will show that adding Bayer’s androgen receptor inhibitor (ARi), NUBEQA® (darolutamide), to standard-of-care androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) and locoregional radiation therapy (RT), improves metastasis-free survival based on conventional imaging (MFS-CI) in prostate cancer patients with high risk of recurrence compared to placebo. These data will be presented at Presidential Symposium I at the ESMO Congress 2026 (LBA4, Saturday, October 24, at 16:30 CEST/10:30 am ET).

NUBEQA is indicated in the U.S. for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) both with and without docetaxel, and for the treatment of adult patients with non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC).1

At a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the interim analysis demonstrated a statistically significant 58% reduction in the risk of metastasis or death with NUBEQA plus ADT and RT compared with placebo plus ADT and RT (hazard ratio [HR] 0.42; 95% CI: 0.27–0.66; p=0.0001).2 The 4-year metastasis-free survival rate was 95% for patients receiving NUBEQA compared with 88% for those receiving placebo.2

“Prostate cancer patients at a high risk of relapse face a considerable risk of recurrence and metastatic spread, making early, effective intervention vital,” said Dr. Tamim Niazi, Associate Professor of Oncology at McGill University, Radiation Oncologist at the Jewish General Hospital in Montreal, Canada, and Co-Lead Investigator of the study. “The improvement in metastasis-free survival seen in interim results from the DASL-HiCaP trial highlights the potential of adding darolutamide to standard androgen deprivation therapy and radiation therapy to help prevent or delay disease progression in patients who are at high risk of progression despite receiving primary curative therapy.”

Secondary endpoints showed NUBEQA was associated with a 53% reduction in the risk of prostate-specific antigen progression or death (PSA-PFS; HR 0.47; 95% CI: 0.33–0.67), and a 4-year PSA-PFS rate of 91% versus 83% with placebo.2 Prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS) and overall survival (OS) hazard ratios were 0.58 (95% CI: 0.17–1.97; 99% vs 99% at 4 years) and 0.88 (95% CI: 0.49–1.59; 97% vs 95% at 4 years), respectively, with follow-up ongoing.2

The safety profile of NUBEQA was consistent with previous studies. The proportions of patients experiencing Grade ≥2 adverse events of special interest for NUBEQA versus placebo were: fatigue/asthenia (14% vs 10%), hypertension (7% vs 9%), fractures (2% vs 3%), and cardiac events (3% vs 3%). Any Grade ≥3 adverse event occurred in 43% of patients in the NUBEQA group versus 36% in the placebo group.2

“These new data underscore the potential of darolutamide to improve outcomes for patients in the early prostate cancer setting, adding to the broad body of evidence helping to support its use across different stages of the disease,” said Christine Roth, Executive Vice President, Global Product Strategy and Commercialization at Bayer’s Pharmaceuticals Division. “Bayer is proud to support research by ANZUP, the Sydney Clinical Trials Centre, Canadian Cancer Trials Group, and international partners, for men with prostate cancer.”

About the DASL-HiCaP trial (ANZUP1801)

The DASL-HiCaP trial is an investigator-initiated, randomized, placebo-controlled, Phase III trial (NCT04136353) evaluating NUBEQA added to standard-of-care ADT and locoregional radiation therapy in prostate cancer patients at high risk of recurrence.

DASL-HiCaP was conducted in collaboration with the University of Sydney and ANZUP Clinical Trials Group and is the fourth Phase III trial for darolutamide to be presented at a prestigious international conference.

A total of 1,106 participants across Australia, New Zealand, Canada, the United States, Ireland and the United Kingdom were randomized 1:1 to receive NUBEQA (600 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 96 weeks, combined with an LHRH analog for 96 weeks and RT to the prostate/prostate bed and pelvic lymph nodes.

The primary endpoint was metastasis-free survival based on conventional imaging (MFS-CI). Secondary endpoints included prostate-specific antigen progression free survival (PSA-PFS), prostate cancer-specific survival (PCSS), and overall survival (OS). The protocol specified an interim analysis after 87 MFS-CI events; follow-up is ongoing to evaluate long-term overall survival.

About NUBEQA® (darolutamide)1

NUBEQA® (darolutamide) is an androgen receptor inhibitor (ARi) with a distinct chemical structure that competitively inhibits androgen binding, AR nuclear translocation, and AR-mediated transcription.

NUBEQA was developed jointly by Bayer and Orion Corporation, a globally operating Finnish pharmaceutical company.

NUBEQA is an androgen receptor inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adult patients with:

  • Non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC)
  • Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC)
  • Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) in combination with docetaxel

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

Warnings & Precautions

Ischemic Heart Disease – Ischemic heart disease, including fatal cases, occurred in patients receiving NUBEQA.

In a pooled analysis of ARAMIS and ARANOTE, ischemic heart disease occurred in 3.4% of patients receiving NUBEQA and 2.2% receiving placebo, including Grade 3-4 events in 1.4% and 0.3%, respectively. Ischemic events led to death in 0.4% of patients receiving NUBEQA and 0.4% receiving placebo.

In ARASENS, ischemic heart disease occurred in 3.2% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel and 2% receiving placebo with docetaxel, including Grade 3-4 events in 1.3% and 1.1%, respectively. Ischemic events led to death in 0.3% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel and 0% receiving placebo with docetaxel.

Monitor for signs and symptoms of ischemic heart disease. Optimize management of cardiovascular risk factors, such as hypertension, diabetes, or dyslipidemia. Discontinue NUBEQA for Grade 3-4 ischemic heart disease.

Seizure – Seizure occurred in patients receiving NUBEQA.

In a pooled analysis of ARAMIS and ARANOTE, Grade 1-3 seizure occurred in 0.2% of patients receiving NUBEQA. Seizure occurred from 261 to 665 days after initiation of NUBEQA.

In ARASENS, seizure occurred in 0.8% of patients receiving NUBEQA with docetaxel, including two Grade 3 events. Seizure occurred from 38 to 1754 days after initiation of NUBEQA.

It is unknown whether anti-epileptic medications will prevent seizures with NUBEQA. Advise patients of the risk of developing a seizure while receiving NUBEQA and of engaging in any activity where sudden loss of consciousness could cause harm to themselves or others. Consider discontinuation of NUBEQA in patients who develop a seizure during treatment.

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity – The safety and efficacy of NUBEQA have not been established in females. NUBEQA can cause fetal harm and loss of pregnancy. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment with NUBEQA and for 1 week after the last dose.

Adverse Reactions

In ARAMIS, serious adverse reactions occurred in 25% of patients receiving NUBEQA and in 20% of patients receiving placebo. Drug Interactions

Effect of Other Drugs on NUBEQA – Concomitant use of NUBEQA with a combined P-gp and strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducer decreases darolutamide exposure which may decrease NUBEQA activity. Avoid concomitant use of NUBEQA with combined P-gp and strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers.

Concomitant use of NUBEQA with a combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitor increases darolutamide exposure which may increase the risk of NUBEQA adverse reactions. Monitor patients more frequently for NUBEQA adverse reactions and modify NUBEQA dosage as needed.

Effects of NUBEQA on Other Drugs – NUBEQA is an inhibitor of BCRP transporter. Concomitant use of NUBEQA increases the AUC and Cmax of BCRP substrates, which may increase the risk of BCRP substrate-related toxicities. Avoid concomitant use with drugs that are BCRP substrates where possible. If used together, monitor patients more frequently for adverse reactions, and consider dose reduction of the BCRP substrate drug.

NUBEQA is an inhibitor of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters. Concomitant use of NUBEQA may increase the plasma concentrations of OATP1B1 or OATP1B3 substrates. Monitor patients more frequently for adverse reactions of these drugs and consider dose reduction while patients are taking NUBEQA.

Key Terms

androgen deprivation therapymedical
Androgen deprivation therapy is a medical treatment that lowers or blocks male hormones (androgens) to slow the growth of hormone-sensitive cancers, most commonly prostate cancer. Think of it as cutting off the fuel a fire needs so the blaze slows; for investors, changes in ADT use, new ADT drugs, or clinical trial results can affect demand for medications, device procedures, safety profiles and long-term revenue for healthcare companies.
hazard ratiotechnical
A hazard ratio is a way scientists compare the chance of something happening over time between two groups, like patients taking different medicines. If the ratio is high, it means one group is more likely to experience the event sooner or more often, which helps determine how effective a treatment is or how risky a situation might be.
metastasis-free survivalmedical
Metastasis-free survival is the length of time after treatment during which a patient shows no signs that cancer has spread to other parts of the body. For investors, it’s a key clinical measure of a drug’s effectiveness — like how long a repair keeps a leak from returning — because longer metastasis-free survival can improve chances of regulatory approval, support stronger sales forecasts, and reduce future treatment costs.
prostate-specific antigen progression free survivalmedical
A clinical-trial endpoint that measures the length of time from a specified start point (for example treatment start or randomization) until biochemical progression of prostate cancer as indicated by rising prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels or death from any cause. The protocol for a trial or regulatory guideline specifies the PSA-based rule that counts as progression (for example a confirmed rise above a baseline or a specified percentage or absolute increase), so the exact numeric threshold and confirmation timing can differ between studies. PSA progression-free survival captures the time without biochemical evidence of disease worsening, but it is a surrogate measure and distinct from endpoints based on symptoms or radiographic tumor progression.

  • New substudy results showed a 51% lower estimated risk of metastasis or death over time with perioperative apalutamide plus ADT compared with immediate surgery

  • Twice as many patients remained free from subsequent treatment at three years with perioperative apalutamide plus ADT compared with surgery alone

  • Results evaluated outcomes versus surgery alone, building on the primary results presented at ASCO 2026

NEW BRUNSWICK, N.J., Oct. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) today announced new results from the Phase 3 PROTEUS substudy that directly compared the investigational use of apalutamide plus androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), given for six months before and after surgery, with radical prostatectomy alone in patients with high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer. The apalutamide plus ADT regimen reduced the risk of disease recurrence or death by 62 percent compared with surgery alone. The regimen also showed a numerical improvement in metastasis-free survival (MFS), with a 51 percent lower risk of metastasis or death. Patients receiving apalutamide plus ADT also went longer before needing subsequent therapy.1

These substudy findings build on the primary PROTEUS results presented during the plenary session of the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Annual Meeting and evaluate a remaining clinical question by directly comparing perioperative apalutamide plus ADT with surgery alone, a longstanding standard of care.1,2

The new results were presented as a late-breaking abstract in a proffered paper session at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 (#LBA53). The accompanying manuscript has been accepted for publication by European Urology.1

The burden of recurrence in high-risk localized prostate cancer

For patients with high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer, surgery has long been a standard of care performed with curative intent. Yet nearly half of patients will see their cancer return and require additional treatment.3,4 Recurrence can mean facing further therapy and the continued risk that the disease will spread, underscoring the need for approaches that can improve outcomes earlier in the course of disease.5

Apalutamide blocks androgen hormones from binding to their receptor, which can help slow prostate cancer progression. It is currently approved for use in advanced prostate cancer, including cases where the disease has spread (metastatic castration-sensitive) or is no longer responding to certain hormone therapies (non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer).6

Expert and company perspectives on improving outcomes earlier in high-risk prostate cancer 

"Radical prostatectomy has long been a cornerstone of curative-intent treatment for high-risk localized prostate cancer, yet recurrence remains a concern for patients with aggressive disease," said Alberto Briganti, M.D.,* Professor of Urology and Urologic Surgeon at IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital, Milan. "In this substudy, median event-free survival was 19.1 months with surgery alone, highlighting the challenges these patients continue to face despite treatment intended to cure their cancer. The reduction in the risk of recurrence and metastases after radical prostatectomy seen with apalutamide plus androgen deprivation therapy suggests we may be able to build on surgery and help more patients achieve lasting disease control."

"For people with high-risk early prostate cancer, finishing surgery doesn't necessarily mean the uncertainty is over. The possibility of recurrence can weigh heavily on patients and their families, even as they try to move forward with their lives," said Courtney Bugler,† President and CEO of ZERO Prostate Cancer, a leading prostate cancer patient advocacy organization in the U.S. "The possibility of helping more people remain free from disease recurrence, and potentially avoid or delay additional treatment, is incredibly meaningful. More time without another treatment can mean more time focused on family, work and life, rather than what comes next for their cancer."

"The primary PROTEUS study showed the potential of treating high-risk prostate cancer earlier with apalutamide plus androgen deprivation therapy. We designed this substudy to take that evidence further by evaluating the regimen against surgery alone, a longstanding standard of care for these patients," said Yusri Elsayed, M.D., M.H.Sc., Ph.D., Global Therapeutic Area Head, Oncology, Johnson & Johnson. "These findings provide important additional insight into what this approach could mean for patients and reinforce why we continue to investigate ways to improve outcomes earlier in the course of disease."

Perioperative treatment demonstrates improvement in event-free survival

The PROTEUS substudy evaluated apalutamide plus ADT before and after surgery compared with radical prostatectomy alone in 408 patients with newly diagnosed, non-metastatic, high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer who were fit for surgery and systemic therapy. The primary endpoint was event-free survival (EFS), defined as the time to biochemical failure, local or regional recurrence, distant metastasis or death.1

At a median follow-up of 37.8 months, apalutamide plus ADT significantly improved EFS, reducing the risk of recurrence or death by 62 percent compared with surgery alone (hazard ratio [HR], 0.38; 95 percent confidence interval [CI], 0.26-0.55; p<0.0001). Median EFS was not reached with apalutamide plus ADT, compared with 19.1 months with surgery alone. At three years, 63 percent of patients receiving apalutamide plus ADT remained event-free compared with 41.4 percent of those undergoing surgery alone.1

Numerical improvements were also observed across secondary and exploratory endpoints. For the secondary endpoint of MFS, apalutamide plus ADT showed a 51 percent lower risk of distant metastasis or death (HR, 0.49; 95 percent CI, 0.26-0.90; nominal p=0.0193). For the exploratory endpoint of time to first subsequent therapy, the regimen showed a 71 percent lower risk of needing subsequent treatment (HR, 0.29; 95 percent CI, 0.20-0.43; nominal p<0.0001). At three years, 64.6 percent of patients receiving apalutamide plus ADT remained free from subsequent therapy compared with 32 percent undergoing surgery alone. Additional follow-up is underway to evaluate overall survival.1

The safety profile was consistent with the primary PROTEUS study results. Grade 3 or 4 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 31 percent of patients receiving apalutamide plus ADT and 22 percent receiving surgery alone. No treatment-emergent adverse events leading to death were reported in either arm. The most common adverse events with apalutamide included hot flush (64 percent) and urinary incontinence (63 percent).1

Apalutamide plus ADT has not been approved by regulatory authorities for the treatment of high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer. These findings add to the growing body of evidence evaluating the potential of treating selected patients with high-risk prostate cancer earlier in the course of disease.

About the PROTEUS substudy

The PROTEUS substudy is a randomized, open-label study evaluating perioperative apalutamide plus androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) compared with radical prostatectomy alone in patients with high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer who are candidates for radical prostatectomy. The substudy was designed to further evaluate the efficacy and safety of adding apalutamide plus ADT before and after surgery compared with surgery alone.7

A total of 408 patients were randomized to one of two treatment groups, with 102 receiving apalutamide plus ADT and 306 undergoing radical prostatectomy alone. Patients receiving apalutamide plus ADT were treated for six 28-day cycles before radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection and for six cycles after surgery, with apalutamide paused two weeks before and resumed four weeks after radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection. Apalutamide was administered orally at 240 mg once daily. Patients in the comparator arm underwent radical prostatectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection followed by standard institutional practice or observation.7

The primary endpoint is event-free survival (EFS), defined as the time to biochemical failure, local or regional recurrence, distant metastasis or death. Secondary endpoints include prostate-specific antigen (PSA)-free survival and metastasis-free survival (MFS), with exploratory endpoints including time to first subsequent systemic therapy and overall survival.7

About high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer

Approximately 330,000 people are diagnosed with prostate cancer each year in the U.S.8 Up to 40 percent of patients will be classified as high-risk.9 Despite advancements in treatment, disease recurrence remains common in patients with high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer. Real-world data show that approximately half of patients undergoing prostatectomy experience recurrence, metastasis or death within five years. Patients with high-risk disease also face increased risk of requiring additional therapy, metastatic progression and death from prostate cancer.4 It's estimated that more than 36,000 patients will succumb to prostate cancer in 2026, which reinforces the importance of choosing the best possible therapy early for patients with advanced prostate cancer.9,10

About ERLEADA

ERLEADA (apalutamide) is an androgen receptor inhibitor indicated for the treatment of patients with non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC) and for the treatment of patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC). ERLEADA received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for nmCRPC in February 2018 and received U.S. FDA approval for mCSPC in September 2019. ERLEADA is the first and only next-generation androgen receptor inhibitor offering a once-daily, single-tablet treatment option for patients. To date, more than 380,000 patients worldwide have been treated with ERLEADA. Additional studies are ongoing to evaluate ERLEADA in earlier stages of prostate cancer, including high-risk localized and locally advanced disease.

The legal manufacturer for ERLEADA is Janssen Biotech, Inc. For more information, visit https://www.jnj.com/.

ERLEADA INDICATIONS AND IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION6

INDICATIONS

ERLEADA® (apalutamide) is an androgen receptor inhibitor indicated for the treatment of patients with:

  • Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC)

  • Non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC)

WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS

Cerebrovascular and Ischemic Cardiovascular Events, including events leading to death, occurred in patients receiving ERLEADA. Monitor for signs and symptoms of ischemic heart disease and cerebrovascular disorders. Optimize management of cardiovascular risk factors, such as hypertension, diabetes, or dyslipidemia. Consider discontinuation of ERLEADA for Grade 3 and 4 events.

In a randomized study (SPARTAN) of patients with nmCRPC, ischemic cardiovascular events occurred in 3.7% of patients treated with ERLEADA and 2% of patients treated with placebo. In a randomized study (TITAN) in patients with mCSPC, ischemic cardiovascular events occurred in 4.4% of patients treated with ERLEADA and 1.5% of patients treated with placebo. Across the SPARTAN and TITAN studies, 4 patients (0.3%) treated with ERLEADA and 2 patients (0.2%) treated with placebo died from an ischemic cardiovascular event. Patients with history of unstable angina, myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, stroke, or transient ischemic attack within 6 months of randomization were excluded from the SPARTAN and TITAN studies.

In the SPARTAN study, cerebrovascular events occurred in 2.5% of patients treated with ERLEADA and 1% of patients treated with placebo. In the TITAN study, cerebrovascular events occurred in 1.9% of patients treated with ERLEADA and 2.1% of patients treated with placebo. Across the SPARTAN and TITAN studies, 3 patients (0.2%) treated with ERLEADA and 2 patients (0.2%) treated with placebo died from a cerebrovascular event.

Fractures occurred in patients receiving ERLEADA. Evaluate patients for fracture risk. Monitor and manage patients at risk for fractures according to established treatment guidelines and consider use of bone-targeted agents.

In a randomized study (SPARTAN) of patients with nmCRPC, fractures occurred in 12% of patients treated with ERLEADA and in 7% of patients treated with placebo. In a randomized study (TITAN) of patients with mCSPC, fractures occurred in 9% of patients treated with ERLEADA and in 6% of patients treated with placebo.

Falls occurred in patients receiving ERLEADA with increased frequency in the elderly. Evaluate patients for fall risk.

In a randomized study (SPARTAN), falls occurred in 16% of patients treated with ERLEADA compared with 9% of patients treated with placebo. Falls were not associated with loss of consciousness or seizure.

Seizure occurred in patients receiving ERLEADA. Permanently discontinue ERLEADA in patients who develop a seizure during treatment. It is unknown whether anti-epileptic medications will prevent seizures with ERLEADA. Advise patients of the risk of developing a seizure while receiving ERLEADA and of engaging in any activity where sudden loss of consciousness could cause harm to themselves or others.

In two randomized studies (SPARTAN and TITAN), five patients (0.4%) treated with ERLEADA and one patient treated with placebo (0.1%) experienced a seizure. Seizure occurred from 159 to 650 days after initiation of ERLEADA. Patients with a history of seizure or, predisposing factors for seizure, or receiving drugs known to decrease the seizure threshold or to induce seizure were excluded. There is no clinical experience in re-administering ERLEADA to patients who experienced a seizure.

Severe Cutaneous Adverse Reactions — Fatal and life-threatening cases of severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs), including Stevens–Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN), and drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) occurred in patients receiving ERLEADA.

Monitor patients for the development of SCARs. Advise patients of the signs and symptoms of SCARs (eg, a prodrome of fever, flu-like symptoms, mucosal lesions, progressive skin rash, or lymphadenopathy). If a SCAR is suspected, interrupt ERLEADA until the etiology of the reaction has been determined. Consultation with a dermatologist is recommended. If a SCAR is confirmed, or for other Grade 4 skin reactions, permanently discontinue ERLEADA [see Dosage and Administration (2.2)].

Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD)/Pneumonitis — Fatal and life-threatening interstitial lung disease (ILD) or pneumonitis can occur in patients treated with ERLEADA.

Post-marketing cases of ILD/pneumonitis, including fatal cases, occurred in patients treated with ERLEADA. Across clinical trials (TITAN and SPARTAN, n=1327), 0.8% of patients treated with ERLEADA experienced ILD/pneumonitis, including 0.2% who experienced Grade 3 events [see Adverse Reactions (6.1, 6.2)].

Monitor patients for new or worsening symptoms indicative of ILD/pneumonitis (eg, dyspnea, cough, fever). Immediately withhold ERLEADA if ILD/pneumonitis is suspected. Permanently discontinue ERLEADA in patients with severe ILD/pneumonitis or if no other potential causes of ILD/pneumonitis are identified [see Dosage and Administration (2.2)].

Embryo-Fetal Toxicity — The safety and efficacy of ERLEADA have not been established in females. Based on findings from animals and its mechanism of action, ERLEADA can cause fetal harm and loss of pregnancy when administered to a pregnant female. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose of ERLEADA [see Use in Specific Populations (8.1, 8.3)].

Interference with Immunoassay Measurement of Digoxin

ERLEADA can interfere with certain digoxin immunoassays (e.g., Chemiluminescent Microparticle Immunoassays), resulting in falsely elevated digoxin plasma concentration results. Notify the laboratory conducting the digoxin plasma concentration assay to use an appropriate method in patients receiving ERLEADA and digoxin [see Drug Interactions (7.3)].

ADVERSE REACTIONS

The most common adverse reactions (≥10%) that occurred more frequently in the ERLEADA-treated patients (≥2% over placebo) from the randomized placebo-controlled clinical trials (TITAN and SPARTAN) were fatigue, arthralgia, rash, decreased appetite, fall, weight decreased, hypertension, hot flush, diarrhea, and fracture.

Laboratory Abnormalities — All Grades (Grade 3-4)

  • Hematology — In the TITAN study: white blood cell decreased ERLEADA 27% (0.4%), placebo 19% (0.6%). In the SPARTAN study: anemia ERLEADA 70% (0.4%), placebo 64% (0.5%); leukopenia ERLEADA 47% (0.3%), placebo 29% (0%); lymphopenia ERLEADA 41% (1.8%), placebo 21% (1.6%)

  • Chemistry — In the TITAN study: hypertriglyceridemia ERLEADA 17% (2.5%), placebo 12% (2.3%). In the SPARTAN study: hypercholesterolemia ERLEADA 76% (0.1%), placebo 46% (0%); hyperglycemia ERLEADA 70% (2%), placebo 59% (1.0%); hypertriglyceridemia ERLEADA 67% (1.6%), placebo 49% (0.8%); hyperkalemia ERLEADA 32% (1.9%), placebo 22% (0.5%)

Rash — In 2 randomized studies (SPARTAN and TITAN), rash was most commonly described as macular or maculopapular. Adverse reactions of rash were 26% with ERLEADA vs 8% with placebo. Grade 3 rashes (defined as covering >30% body surface area [BSA]) were reported with ERLEADA treatment (6%) vs placebo (0.5%).

The onset of rash occurred at a median of 83 days. Rash resolved in 78% of patients within a median of 78 days from onset of rash. Rash was commonly managed with oral antihistamines and topical corticosteroids, and 19% of patients received systemic corticosteroids. Dose reduction or dose interruption occurred in 14% and 28% of patients, respectively. Of the patients who had dose interruption, 59% experienced recurrence of rash upon reintroduction of ERLEADA.

Hypothyroidism — In 2 randomized studies (SPARTAN and TITAN), hypothyroidism was reported for 8% of patients treated with ERLEADA and 1.5% of patients treated with placebo based on assessments of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) every 4 months. Elevated TSH occurred in 25% of patients treated with ERLEADA and 7% of patients treated with placebo. The median onset was at the first scheduled assessment. There were no Grade 3 or 4 adverse reactions. Thyroid replacement therapy, when clinically indicated, should be initiated or dose adjusted.

DRUG INTERACTIONS

Effect of Other Drugs on ERLEADA

ERLEADA Strong CYP2C8 or CYP3A4 Inhibitors

Reduce the ERLEADA dose as recommended for adverse reactions [see Dosage and Administration (2.2)]. Co-administration of a strong CYP2C8 or CYP3A4 inhibitor is predicted to increase the steady–state exposure of the active moieties (sum of unbound apalutamide plus the potency–adjusted unbound N-desmethyl-apalutamide).

Effect of ERLEADA on Other Drugs

Substrates of CYP3A4, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, P-gp, BCRP, or OATP1B1

Refer to the Prescribing Information for these substrates. Consider alternative agents when possible or evaluate for loss of activity of the substrate if concomitant use cannot be avoided.

Apalutamide is a strong inducer of CYP3A4 and CYP2C19, a weak inducer of CYP2C9, and an inducer of P-gp, BCRP, and OATP1B1. Apalutamide decreases exposure of substrates of CYP3A4, CYP2C19, CYP2C9, P-gp, BCRP, or OATP1B1, which may decrease the effectiveness of these substrates.

USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS

The recommended ERLEADA dosage in patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) is lower than the recommended dosage in patients with normal hepatic function. No dosage modification is recommended for patients with mild (Child-Pugh A) or moderate (Child-Pugh B) hepatic impairment.

  • Objective response rate of 72.2% among response-evaluable patients receiving a starting dose of ≥450 mg at 32-week landmark
  • Disease control rate of 100% across all response-evaluable patients receiving a starting dose of ≥450 mg, with no disease progression and no treatment discontinuations due to TRAEs
  • Data informed FDA-aligned dose and regimen selection for upcoming PEDESTAL Phase 3 registrational trial, with initiation planned in the first half of 2027 and topline results anticipated in 2029
  • Company to host investor webcast on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00 CEST (12:00 p.m. EDT)

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Parabilis Medicines (Nasdaq: PBLS), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to creating extraordinary medicines for patients with serious diseases by unlocking historically undruggable targets, today announced updated safety and efficacy data for zolucatetide, the first and only direct inhibitor of the β-catenin:TCF interaction, in patients with desmoid tumors. The data were presented today in an oral presentation at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026, taking place October 23–27, 2026, in Madrid, Spain.

The updated results, based on a June 22, 2026, data cutoff, include data from both the dose escalation and dose optimization portions of the ongoing Phase 1/2 trial and reinforce the strong efficacy and favorable safety and tolerability profile observed with zolucatetide. Among response-evaluable patients who began treatment at a starting dose of ≥450 mg, zolucatetide demonstrated an objective response rate (ORR) of 72.2% (13/18) in a 32-week landmark analysis. A disease control rate (DCR) of 100% was observed across all 46 response-evaluable patients who received a starting dose of ≥450 mg, with no disease progression.

Data from a three-arm randomized dose optimization trial supported selection of a 450 mg weekly induction regimen administered for four cycles, followed by 300 mg every two weeks for long-term maintenance. Following productive end-of-Phase 2 discussions, Parabilis has reached alignment with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on the selected dose and regimen, on the use of a placebo-controlled study design, and on progression-free survival (PFS) as the primary endpoint for registrational development.

Parabilis plans to initiate the randomized, double-blind PEDESTAL Phase 3 trial (Phase 3 Evaluation of DESmoid Tumor Activity with zoLucatetide) in the first half of 2027, with topline results anticipated in 2029.

“Desmoid tumors are chronic and life-altering for patients, often affecting people at a young age, and patients need treatments that can deliver rapid, deep and durable tumor responses with a tolerability profile suited for long-term treatment,” said Mathai Mammen, M.D., Ph.D., Chairman, CEO and President of Parabilis Medicines. “We designed zolucatetide to directly inhibit β-catenin:TCF, a historically undruggable target at the heart of the biology driving these tumors. The depth and consistency of responses we are seeing, together with the favorable safety and tolerability profile observed to date, reinforce our conviction that zolucatetide has the potential to deliver a truly differentiated medicine and meaningfully expand the number of patients who can benefit from treatment. We are very pleased with the clarity of the FDA’s feedback on our registrational development strategy, and with our Phase 3 regimen selected, we are moving with urgency to bring this medicine to patients.”

Updated Phase 1/2 Results
As of the June 22, 2026, data cutoff, 76 patients with desmoid tumors had been enrolled and treated across all dose levels in the dose escalation and dose optimization portions of the trial. Median age was 37 years (range 19–80), and 69.7% of patients were female. The population included both patients who had previously been treated with and failed gamma-secretase inhibitors (GSIs) and patients naive to GSIs.

A total of 48 patients began treatment at a starting induction dose of ≥450 mg, prior to down-dosing for maintenance. Two patients were started at 900 mg, but had an average dose of 400–500 mg over the first four months of treatment. Of these 48 patients, 46 were response-evaluable, and 18 had scans at 32 weeks. Median time on treatment for this cohort was 4.7 months (range 0.5–22.3), reflecting recent enrollment of a substantial portion of the cohort.

Efficacy

  • ORR per RECIST 1.1 was 72.2% (13/18) among all patients evaluable at the 32-week landmark
  • A disease control rate (DCR) of 100% was observed across all 46 response-evaluable patients
  • Responses were observed irrespective of prior gamma-secretase inhibitor (GSI) exposure or CTNNB1 or APC mutation status
  • No evidence of disease progression or resistance

Safety

  • Zolucatetide continued to demonstrate a favorable safety and tolerability profile at the selected doses for Phase 3 registrational development
  • Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were predominantly low-grade; the most commonly reported TRAEs were fatigue, alopecia and nausea
  • No patients discontinued treatment due to TRAEs
  • Not associated with ovarian toxicity or high-grade gastrointestinal or skin toxicities commonly reported with GSIs

“The early clinical results with zolucatetide are encouraging, particularly the magnitude and apparent rapidity of tumor responses observed to date,” said Mrinal Gounder, M.D., Sarcoma Medical Oncologist and Early Drug Development Specialist at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, and presenting author of the study. “Desmoid tumors can impose a substantial physical and emotional burden on patients, and therapies capable of achieving meaningful tumor shrinkage while maintaining acceptable tolerability remain an important clinical goal. These findings support further investigation of zolucatetide in the planned Phase 3 trial.”

The Phase 1/2 trial is ongoing in patients with desmoid tumors and a range of other tumor types driven by alterations in the Wnt/β-catenin pathway, and follow-up is continuing. Zolucatetide has received Fast Track and Orphan Drug Designations from the FDA for the treatment of desmoid tumors.

These findings provide further clinical validation of the potential of the Company's Helicon™ platform to unlock disease-driving targets historically considered undruggable.

Investor Webcast
Parabilis will host an investor webcast on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00 CEST (12:00 p.m. EDT) to discuss the updated zolucatetide data that will be presented at ESMO Congress 2026. The webcast will be available on the Investors section of the Parabilis website at https://investors.parabilismed.com. Both the presentation and a replay of the webcast will be available following the event.

About Desmoid Tumors
Desmoid tumors are locally invasive soft-tissue tumors that arise in connective tissues and can be aggressive and recurrent, often causing chronic pain, limited mobility, disfigurement and organ dysfunction. An estimated 30,000 people in the U.S. alone are living with desmoid tumors, including approximately 11,000 who are actively managed, with significant unmet need globally as well. Desmoid tumors typically present in young adults, predominantly females, with many patients requiring prolonged or intermittent treatment. Wnt/β-catenin pathway-activating mutations are the causal driver of desmoid tumors, yet no approved therapies directly target this underlying biology of the disease.

About Zolucatetide
Zolucatetide is an investigational first-in-class and first and only direct inhibitor of the interaction between β-catenin and the T-cell factor (TCF) family of transcription factors, a genetically validated driver of numerous cancers and other serious diseases that has long been considered undruggable. Developed using Parabilis’ Helicon™ peptide platform, zolucatetide is designed to prevent the activation of disease-driving genes by directly targeting β-catenin:TCF, a key downstream node in the Wnt/β-catenin pathway. This approach has the potential to address aberrant Wnt/β-catenin signaling regardless of the upstream APC or β-catenin mutations driving pathway activation, potentially overcoming a key limitation of approaches targeting earlier steps in the pathway.

Zolucatetide is currently being evaluated in an ongoing Phase 1/2 clinical trial (NCT05919264) across a range of indications, including desmoid tumors, familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma (ACP), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and additional Wnt-driven tumor types.

About Parabilis Medicines
Parabilis Medicines (Nasdaq: PBLS) is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company dedicated to creating extraordinary medicines for patients with serious diseases by unlocking biologically important targets long considered undruggable. The Company has pioneered a new class of alpha-helical peptides – Helicons™ – capable of modulating intracellular proteins that have historically been beyond the reach of conventional medicines. The Company's lead investigational medicine, zolucatetide, is the first and only direct inhibitor of the β-catenin:TCF interaction, a central node in the Wnt/β-catenin pathway that has eluded drug developers for decades. Zolucatetide is being evaluated in the clinic across multiple Wnt/β-catenin-driven diseases, including desmoid tumors, familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma (ACP), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and a range of other rare and common solid tumor indications. Beyond zolucatetide, Parabilis is pursuing a follow-on β-catenin degrader program and advancing additional Helicon-based programs focused on other challenging targets, including ERG and allosteric ARON in prostate cancer, where we believe our medicines could have life-altering impact.
